articles.title: WWE SmackDown results, grades (Oct. 23): Chelsea Green beats Roxanne Perez, Michin & B-Fab win tag titles
articles.summary: "WWE SmackDown" was in Ontario, with two title matches and a street fight. Here are the full results, grades and highlights.
articles.body: "WWE SmackDown" was in Ontario, Canada on Friday, with two title matches and a street fight. Gold changed hands in one match, but it ultimately raised more questions than answers.A disaster of richesOutside of the men's tag-team match that never really happened, tonight's "SmackDown" could have been a great show. Instead, it missed the mark on virtually every front. So, we're going to do something a little different tonight: Our best rapid-fire paper-wad-throwing into the flaming trash bin, if you will.Green light to nowhere. Listen, I'm all for Chelsea Green winning. It's overdue for the champion to win matches. What a concept, right? But if you're going to do this Roxanne Perez title match, why have Perez lose? So The Judgment Day can continue forever? To let Tiffany Stratton repeat the exact same story she did with her first Money in the Bank cash-in? The answers appear to be yes to both after the tease that following an expectedly overbooked match. And neither are exciting. To make the booking around the Women's Championship all the more absurd, Nikki Bella — who lost to Paige last week — will challenge Green for the title next week. It's almost as if WWE intentionally tried to make tonight's show bad..@RaquelWWE and @roxanne_wwe were NOT letting that happen 😤 pic.twitter.com/hNbJhTLzci— WWE (@WWE) October 24, 2026 Fun while it lasted. Well, at least I get to say I interviewed Tatum Paxley while she was a champion for two whole weeks. She and Alexa Bliss lost the Women's Tag Team titles tonight. In their first defense. Against B-Fab & Michin. With interference from Jade Cargill. Paxley took the pin. It seems nothing was learned from Sol Ruca's main roster start on "Raw," because this decision reeked of that situation, which is horrific for Paxley. She'll likely be fine in the end, but Fatal Influence dropping the titles made it all meaningless. What was the point of Paxley and Bliss holding the titles? So Paxley and Charlotte Flair can win them? I don't know, but it's dumb and damaging to everyone involved — except the people who never should have become a stable in the first place and now hold the titles.NEW TAG TEAM CHAMPS! @MiaYim and @TheVibeBri got some new gold 🏆 pic.twitter.com/PmxzL18up0— WWE (@WWE) October 24, 2026 Sleep fight. Somehow, Blake Monroe and Giulia managed to deliver the most boring "Street Fight" match of all time. While impressive, it must be clarified that it's not entirely their fault. Outside of a suplex-onto-the-chairs spot, the crowd was dead for this match. That was the case for the whole show, really. Randy Orton was the only one who really got Ontario moving. With Monroe, we're in a tough spot where suspension of disbelief is almost impossible, given the violent work she did in AEW. In this match, Giulia threw her into a mirror — glass — and there wasn't a single cut on her. No blood. Nothing. We're all for safety, but it's so unrealistic that it's silly. The whole effect is diminished at that point. It was just a slow match that felt like a playground tussle, hopefully moving Monroe onward. Unfortunately, hope has been lost for Giulia.Quick mirror break...literally! 😬 pic.twitter.com/C1GOx0QFAs— WWE (@WWE) October 24, 2026 False advertisement. I'm trying to keep this short, and I don't even know where to begin. U.S. Champion Trick Williams is fully going after Sami Zayn now (again), and will challenge for Zayn's world title next week. Before that, however, a completely random match between Williams and Rey Fenix against Zayn and Johnny Gargano was set up for tonight's main event. Still, no one cares about reviving the Williams-Zayn feud after how awful it got toward the end. But tonight's tag match never even really happened, as Ricky Saints ended it almost immediately with an attack on Fenix to bring in Penta for a trios match. There was no reason they couldn't have just set that up in the opening segment instead of the tag match. Unless Penta is secretly the dumbest human on the planet, no one thought he was cashing in while Zayn, Gargano and Saints were beating down his brother and Williams..@PENTAELZEROM has entered the chat! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/sCD3sYReR2— WWE (@WWE) October 24, 2026 More false advertisement. Unlike the Zayn business, WWE actually posted pre-show that The MFTs would take on Bakusai in a non-title match. What actually happened was a brawl in the rampway that not a soul gave a damn about. It is depressing how quickly WWE has reduced its entire tag division into irrelevancy. There is less than zero reason to care about any of this, and the teams aren't even good. I'm not sure what would've been worse: Actually getting the match or what transpired instead.This is nothing but CHAOS 😱 pic.twitter.com/y5ivxACiR9— WWE (@WWE) October 24, 2026 Beefin'. The lone bright spots on this show came from all the most experienced, biggest stars available. Who would have thought? Cody Rhodes, Randy Orton, CM Punk and Kevin Owens all delivered pretty solid interactions that got you interested in seeing them again. With the latter, it was a bit of a corny exchange, like two middle-schoolers trying to insult each other. But Orton and Rhodes hyping up their Last Man Standing match at Crown Jewel was everything you'd expect.Will @CMPunk and @FightOwensFight finally settle the score in TWO WEEKS in Brooklyn?! 🤔 pic.twitter.com/u2ygaeK78p— WWE (@WWE) October 24, 2026 Gone missing. Have you heard of Gunther or Finn Balor? You know, roster staples who've been around for years. Two guys recently involved in world title pictures. They've been feuding with each other, somewhat in the background of their title pursuits. Yet they were nowhere to be seen tonight.How the mighty fall.Unlike on "Raw," it's at least nice to see stars and champions actually wrestle on a weekly show. I give Friday's "SmackDown" a crown score of: 👑 1/10 👑WWE SmackDown full card results and grades:Trick Williams and The Lucha Bros (Penta and Rey Fenix) def. Sami Zayn, Johnny Gargano and Ricky Saints — 👑 2.75/5 👑Women's Tag Team Championship: Michin & B-Fab def. Tatum Paxley & Alexa Bliss (c.) — 👑 1.75/5 👑Street Fight: Blake Monroe def. Giulia — 👑 2.25/5 👑Women's Championship: Chelsea Green (c) def. Roxanne Perez — 👑 2/5 👑Recap "SmackDown" with Uncrowned's live blog:

articles.title: It’s time to find a new browser
articles.summary: Plus: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Wildwood, Claude Duet, and more in this week’s Installer.
articles.body: Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 149, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, happy It Actually Feels Like Fall Now At Least In My Neighborhood), and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.) This week, I’ve been reading about Demis Hassabis and computer chips and permafrost, enjoying the first episodes of Machine Gods, filming the next season of Version History (pet season!), seeing You Can See Everything and then reading and listening to absolutely everything about it, painstakingly updating all the stuff in my 1Password, making tiny documents with Tiny Little Office, watching Conan O’Brien own Subway Takes the way he once owned Hot Ones, finally getting properly good at CapCut, and blasting the soundtrack to The Mandalorian and Grogu all workday long. I also have for you a new AI assistant, the most Duo-y new app for the iPhone Duo, my hunt for the next great browser, and much more. Let’s do this. (As always, the best part of Installer is your ideas and tips. What are you playing / reading / watching / listening to / modding with Claude this week? Tell me everything: installer@theverge.com. And if you know someone else who might enjoy Installer, forward it to them and tell them to subscribe here.) The Drop * Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Obviously, Grand Theft Auto VI is the biggest game release of the year, but a new COD is always a big deal. This one doesn’t sound like some grand reinvention of the form, but rather an even more playable, even more powerful version of what works. I was particularly excited to hear that the campaign mode is a huge improvement this time. * The Blink Mini 4K. Ring cameras get a lot more shine, but Amazon’s cheaper brand also makes some pretty good stuff. This one’s part of a whole new lineup of devices, but $80 for a 4K camera with two-way audio and plenty of smart security features? Not a bad deal. * JustWatch TV. As streaming services get incessantly more expensive, I’m starting to bail on some paid services and spend more time on the free ones. JustWatch’s new service is surprisingly well-stocked out of the gate — I suspect they’ve been watching what people search for, and making some smart content bets. * Claude Duet. Here’s Anthropic’s answer to Muse, Instinct, and Dots. Duet seems to be focused on helping you get stuff done at work by making to-do lists, coordinating meetings, and compiling data for you. Still waitlist-only right now, but it’ll be interesting to see if it’s as thirsty for attention as Muse is. * Wildwood. Before you see this gorgeous, by all accounts excellent stop-motion movie, read everything you can about how it was made. Not a pixel of generative AI in sight, just an unbelievable amount of hard work and human creativity. Humans rock, artists rock, this movie rocks. * The Teenage Engineering EP-35. When you go to buy this thing, it’s technically called “Life is fantastic!” Which, sure. This thing is a battery powered, multi-input, multi-instrument amp with lots of effects. As always, it is extremely cool-looking. I have no use for it, and I want it quite badly. * Nintendo Switch Sports Resort. Nintendo basically hasn’t changed the formula here since Wii Sports from two decades ago, and I have absolutely no problem with that. Anything that gives me that super-active tennis and bowling (plus volleyball, boxing, thumb wrestling, and more) is a win in my book. * Delta 2.0. The next couple of weeks are going to be full of interesting app updates as developers try to figure out what to make of Apple’s foldable phone. But one of the best is already available; Delta can now pretty successfully cosplay as any handheld console ever. (Plus the Sega Genesis!) * Kindle Plus. This is mostly just a rebranding of Kindle Unlimited, but Amazon put a couple of interesting new features in its $12 monthly reading subscription, including AI-narrated audiobooks. I am dubious of those, but excited about expanding access to audiobooks. We’ll see. Spotlight The worst news of the week here in the Installerverse is that Arc is going away. This was obviously coming: The Browser Company bailed on Arc two years ago in favor of the more AI-centric Dia, and Arc has been in maintenance mode ever since. But now it’s not just being ignored, it’s going away. By Christmas, you won’t even be able to use the app anymore. So now a lot of us are stuck looking for another browser. There are a million new ones out there, many of them somewhere between “heavily inspired by Arc” and “a direct copy of Arc I made in Codex this morning.” I need to test a lot of them. I don’t know exactly where I’ll land yet, but I figured I’d share a bunch of the ones I’m looking at: * Dia. It has recently gotten a lot of Arc’s best features, and some of the AI stuff is pretty cool. (And mercifully easy to turn off.) The Browser Company’s attention to aesthetic detail remains the best in the biz, so I’m starting here. * Zen. A total ripoff of Arc, and I mean that as a compliment. Zen runs on Mozilla’s Gecko engine rather than Chromium, which is a win for anyone looking for a little less Google influence in their lives. Last time I tried Zen it was a little buggy and unpolished, but I’ve heard it’s come a long way. * Orion. I am a dedicated and very happy Kagi user, and I’ve heard good things about how simple and resource-friendly the company’s browser is. Given the seamless Kagi integration, I sort of hope this one wins for me. * Vivaldi. I used Vivaldi for a while, and I love how customizable it is. I eventually got it set up exactly the way I wanted it. But right next to all that customization is just a feeling of fiddliness, and I couldn’t quite get comfortable in the browser. Might try again. * Helium. The opposite of Vivaldi, this is a super minimalist, no-frills browser. It’s probably what I need, honestly. * Firefox. Its confusing stance on AI aside, I like a lot of the recent design and feature choices Firefox has made. I’m also intrigued by some of the Firefox forks, like Waterfox and Floorp, which give it even more customization options. * Brave. Brave has always felt too heavy to me, and like it’s always trying to convince me to use more of its own proprietary (and often underpowered) features. But it seems to always win in privacy comparisons, so I might need to give it a go again. On mobile, it’s easy. Quiche is my favorite iOS browser by a mile. Arc was never great on Android, so I’m betting most of us never switched there in the first place. There are also the default browsers, of course, like Chrome, Safari, and Edge. But each of those browsers continues to fail me in one way or another, and so my search continues. If you’ve found your browser of the future, tell me all about it! Otherwise, I’ll report back here periodically through my journey. Crowdsourced Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com or message me on Signal — @davidpierce.11 — with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on Threads and this post on Bluesky. “Youth is an absolute SCREAM on HBO Max at the moment.” — Jonathan “Todoist has a stellar integration with Siri AI that has finally made me fully commit to just using it If you delete Reminders, Todoist becomes the default on Siri AI and you can add a to-do to any project with tag AND location support (using Apple Maps saved locations like home and work!). The best part is that it all works WITHOUT having to say ‘... in todoist’ at the end of each query!” — Sajishnu “Apple added Sound Glow to existing HomePod models and it’s just kinda fun to watch the light on top of HomePod glow and flash. So I’m doing that with some of my favorite playlists.” — Connor “I’m reading a book called How to Read a Book by Mortimer J. Adler because I want to get better at analysis and reading for understanding vs. absorbing basic information.” — Rhoades “My girlfriend took a train ride up the west coast and reported that no less than four different people asked her if her 2024 Samsung Galaxy Z-Flip 6 was the new iPhone Duo.” — Nicholas “I recently read Bodies of Magic by Freya Marske, and it was excellent. What if med school was magical, but everyone was still sleeping with each other and stressing over student loans? Then an unexpected dead body shows up during finals.” — Emmett “I got a Framework Laptop 13 Pro running Ubuntu last month, and I’m really happy with it. (I haven’t done anything with Linux in maybe 20 years — it’s come a long way!) So now I’m trying to see if I can replace Capture One with Darktable. If I can, that would break my last tie to macOS, and I’ll replace my iMac with a Framework Desktop.” — Morgan “Exploring the new Nektropos Castle dungeon in EverQuest Legends. The game has been such a nostalgia trip back to 1999, but new content in an ancient game is a bizarre delight.” — Alex “Setting up Navidrome and having Claude build me a definitive ‘Songs From the Black Hole’ playlist from my Weezer MP3 collection. (It’s harder than first appears: is ‘Lisa’ track 12 or not!?)” — Micheal “Best Buy had a pretty insane deal on a Bambu A1 Mini, so we got my 12 year old son a 3D printer for his birthday. It’s amazing how easy it was to put out a seemingly perfectly accurate PLA print, compared to horror stories from older printers.” — Jeff Signing off Last week, my wife and I went car shopping. Our plan was just to drive a bunch of cars — we knew we needed something with three rows, and really had no experience with any of them — and then go home. Somehow, a few hours later, we were the proud and slightly bewildered owners of a new Kia Carnival. So far the car has been great, but wow are there a lot of weird tech ideas in cars now. I’m good with CarPlay and Android Auto. I hate how much everything has become a touchscreen. But I’m most thrown by how many features of my car now exist in a companion app. How do we feel about this? I almost miss when I had no idea what to do about the check engine light. Anyway, I’m a minivan dad now. I think I’m okay with it. Send car tips! Send minivan tips! Send help! See you next week!

articles.body: Uncrowned has Dalton Smith vs. Alberto Puello live results, round-by-round updates, highlights, ring walks and start time for the Smith vs. Puello fight card on Saturday at Utilita Arena in Sheffield, England. In the night's main event, Dalton Smith defends his WBC super lightweight title against former two-time champion Alberto Puello.Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) stopped Subriel Matias in New York in January to capture the championship. He now returns to his hometown for his first title defense. articles.title: Valkyries even WNBA Finals with 67-62 win over Dream in Game 4 behind 17 points from Gabby Williams
articles.summary: Golden State increased the pace and frustrated Atlanta inside with tenacious defense, pushing the series to 2-2.
articles.body: The WNBA Finals are tied at 2-2 after the Golden State Valkyries responded with their best performance of the series for a 67-62 win over the Dream in Game 4 on Saturday in Atlanta.Game 5 will be Monday in San Francisco at 8 p.m. ET. Gabby Williams scored 17, while Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton each added 13 to lead Golden State. Hayes' contribution was especially notable with Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase changing the starting lineup, swapping Hayes and Kaila Charles for Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini. "I just wanted to change it up. The best thing about our team is, like, no one cares who starts," Nakase said after the game. "No one cares. People on the bench. It doesn't matter. We can do that because they're a really selfless team, egoless team."Golden State missed its first six shots before taking control of the game with a 12-0 run in the first quarter to take a 16-11 lead. The Dream pushed back in the second but each time they got close, Burton would hit a basket to keep Atlanta at a distance. The Valkyries outscored the Dream 26-15 in the second quarter to take a 42-26 lead into halftime.Atlanta got 19 points from Rhyne Howard, but couldn't get enough from the rest of the lineup. Jordin Canada and Isobel Borlase both contributed 10 points, but Allisha Gray tallied only 5 points while dealing with her hand injury and foul trouble that restricted her to 22 minutes. Additionally, Angel Reese scored 8 points and had 6 turnovers to go with her 9 rebounds and 3 blocks after recording double-doubles in each of the series' first three games. Reese shot 2 of 12 from the floor and also missed her only 3-point attempt in what's become a key factor for the Dream throughout the regular season and playoffs. "I think I rushed a lot on my shots," Reese said afterward. "I didn't take my time and finish around the basket like I'd been doing the last three games." Golden State pushed the pace to prevent the Dream from utilizing its frontcourt advantage (notably Reese). The Valkyries shot 36% overall, but took 72 shots to Atlanta's 54 (on 33% shooting), creating multiple scoring opportunities. The Dream also contributed to the Valkyries' effort by committing 17 turnovers.The Valkyries also played more physically inside, frustrating Atlanta and leading to several confrontations between Reese and Golden State's Kiah Stokes and Hayes. That may have taken Reese out of her game, as her numbers demonstrated."The goal when we play on the road is just to steal a win," Stokes said after the game. The 11-year veteran had 3 blocks or more for the fourth consecutive game, setting a record for a WNBA Finals with 14 so far in the series.The 2026 WNBA Finals are now a best-of-three series with two of those games set to be played on the Valkyries' home court at Chase Center in San Francisco, beginning with Monday's Game 5. As Yahoo Sports' Cassandra Negley pointed out during the live updates of Saturday's matchup, the Valkyries ensuring that a Game 6 will be necessary in this series causes some logistical issues. Atlanta's State Farm Arena will be unavailable Thursday, as the NBA's Atlanta Hawks have a home game. The Dream and WNBA were able to make arrangements to play Games 3 and 4 at the larger venue after it initially wasn't available, but that likely won't be possible for the last game to be played in Atlanta for this series.

articles.summary: Here's everything you need to know injury-wise for Week 7 of the NFL season.
articles.body: Week 7 is underway, and we're tracking all the injuries before game time.Jump to a team:AFC East: Bills (bye) | Dolphins | Patriots (played Thurs.) | JetsAFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | SteelersAFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars (bye) | TitansAFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers (bye)NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders (bye)NFC North: Bears (played Thurs.) | Lions | Packers | VikingsNFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | BuccaneersNFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | SeahawksLive injury updatesTwo star players who have each missed the past two weeks were back at practice for their respective teams.The Philadelphia Eagles welcomed back Saquon Barkley after he's been out since Week 4 due to a hamstring injury. The running back is now considered questionable for a "Monday Night Football" clash with the Dallas Cowboys.Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was also back on the practice field, albeit in a limited capacity, but the Ravens announced Saturday that they've downgraded him from questionable to out for their Sunday showdown with the Cincinnati Bengals. As a result, Jackson will miss his third consecutive game with a high ankle sprain.There was a worrying sign for the Los Angeles Rams on Thursday as wide receiver Puka Nacua left practice with a calf injury. He did not take part on Friday and head coach Sean McVay said Nacua will be listed as questionable against the Las Vegas Raiders. LA will already be without Davante Adams due to a hamstring injury.Nacua has already missed two games this season with a psoas injury.Other Week 7 injuries to monitor:San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf) did not practice on Thursday or Friday. Bosa has not practiced for almost a month after pulling his calf in practice and has already missed four games with the injury.New York Jets running back Breece Hall (quad) returned to practice on Thursday. While he was a limited participant, it's an encouraging sign for Hall, who has missed three games with the injury. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.The Arizona Cardinals will not have Jeremiyah Love (ankle) available to them this week against the Denver Broncos. The running back will be sidelined for a second straight game. Head coach Mike LaFleur told the media last week that an injured reserve stint had not been discussed for Love.Baker Mayfield (thumb) is expected to return this week for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The quarterback has been out since injuring the digit in Week 3. He will not have Emeka Egbuka as one of his available weapons. The wide receiver was at practice on Friday, but remains in concussion protocol and is out for Sunday.While the Houston Texans won't have running back David Montgomery (groin) against the New York Giants, they will be getting back Tank Dell. articles.summary: After an upset-filled Saturday of action in Week 7, what does this week have in store?
articles.body: Don't sleep on Week 8 just because there are only two games between ranked opponents on Saturday. The early window already delivered an upset as unranked Cincinnati knocked off No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24, handing the Red Raiders their first loss of the season.Meanwhile, No. 6 Indiana survived a big scare in the Big House, eking out a 13-6 overtime win over Michigan.Still to come, the SEC has a pair of intriguing games in the afternoon window with Texas A&M facing No. 13 Alabama and No. 11 Tennessee taking on South Carolina. The Gamecocks are actually favored over the Vols.In the evening, No. 7 Ole Miss heads to Austin to meet No. 19 Texas in a game that feels like a must-win for Arch Manning, Steve Sarkisian and the Longhorns.
